claim: pw23's rsk2 (7.5 us kernel + 0.9 us memset at m=128) is latency- and tail-bound with mma.sync at ~25% issue, and its m=256 dual-block variant loses to cuBLASLt. pw29 adds rwk, a wgmma rewrite of the same split-K router: CTA = 64 router rows as the wgmma M (W as A) x 128 or 256 tokens as N, one warpgroup, both operands from 128B-swizzled K-major smem via descriptors, hi and lo as two wgmmas per k16 step into one fp32 accumulator (32 m64n128k16 per CTA at KR 256 instead of 512 mma.sync per warp), 4 or 8 cp.async stages of the K slice issued up front (or a 64-k slot ring for KR 512), and an smem-staged epilogue that reduces with 16-B red.global.add.v4.f32 (half the reds of pw23's v2) into the memset-zeroed output. m=256 holds both token blocks in one CTA (m64n256k16, or two n128 sets) sharing the W tiles. Expected router m=128 about 5 kernel-us (-1.5 to -2.5 judge-us) and m=256 under cuBLASLt's 8.1 kernel-us.
paths: router m=128: pw23's rs64k32 / rp64k32s4 / rp64k32s2 / rp64k64x2 / rp64k32sc (unchanged in-run references) + rw64k32s4 (KR 256, 4 stages, 128 CTAs, 129 KB), rw64k32s8 (8 stages), rw64k64s4x2 (KR 128, 4 stages, 256 CTAs at 2/SM), rw64k16r6 (KR 512, 64 CTAs, ring of 6 64-k slots). router m=256: pw23's rs64k32 / rv64k32 / rv64k64x2 / rv64k32sc + rw64k32s8 and rw64k64s4x2 as two 128-token blocks (256 / 512 CTAs), rwv64k32s4 / rwv64k32s8 (TOKS 256, m64n256k16, 128 CTAs, 193 KB), rwv64k64s4x2 (KR 128, 256 CTAs at 2/SM), rwv64k32s8h2 (two n128 accumulator sets), rwv64k16r4 (KR 512, 64 CTAs, ring of 4). All against r6's cuBLASLt. rwk lives in its own load_inline extension (rw29_*) with -gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a -DNDEBUG; a build failure drops only the rw paths (PREP rw build failed). Same validation as pw23 (one-hot x8 bit-exact vs hi+lo, random rows 2e-5, odd m 121 / 250); served only at m exactly 128 / 256 (_bk).
target_shapes: router m=128: best rw path >= 1.5 us under rp64k32s4 in the same bake (pw23: 13.44-13.89 in-prepare)
router m=256: an rw path under r6 (15.6-15.8 in-prepare)
kill_if: router m=128 best new (rw) path not >= 1.5 us under pw23's rp64k32s4 in the same bake
local_checks: nvcc 12.8 with the file's RWFLAGS (-O3 -lineinfo -gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a -DNDEBUG) -Xptxas -v on the generated source (torch binding swapped for a plain-pointer entry point; device code identical): 9 rwk instances, 0 spills, no 'serialized' warning, no injected warpgroup.arrive; regs 90 (TOKS 128), 140 (TOKS 128 ring), 154 (TOKS 256), 255 (TOKS 256 ring). SASS: HGMMA.64x128x16 / 64x256x16 with both operands gdesc, zero-init folded into the first HGMMA (RZ, !UPT), one DEPBAR.LE + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S + BAR.SYNC per stage, one WARPGROUP.DEPBAR at the end, REDG.E.ADD.F32x4. proj_rsi/tools/rw_emu.py (new) emulates the cp.async staging, descriptor decode (PTX format, SW128 address XOR), ring slot reuse with cp.async landing at issue and at retire, PTX D fragments, the staging epilogue and the v4 reductions: bit-exact one-hot and 3.7e-8 random for all 9 variants at m 128/121/200 (TOKS 128) and 256/250/300 (TOKS 256, partial second blocks), raw smem base 0 and 400; negative controls caught (unswizzled writes, SBO 512, ring wait one group short). GVCU / CUDA strings unchanged from pw23 (r6's 78 gv instances and rsk / rsk2 identical). lint ok (expected multi-build sm_90a warning); cpu-check --official 9/9; CPU mock of _rsbake runs and dispatches every variant (0, 5-11, 100-103, 110-114).
risks: Compile time: one more load_inline build (9 wgmma instances, ~8 s of nvcc locally without torch headers; est. 30-50 s on the judge) on top of pw23's ~105 s prepare; the build is skipped if fewer than 60 s of budget remain.
The kernel uses 128 threads at 1 CTA/SM (TOKS 128 KR 256): every cp.async is issued by 4 warps; if the LSU issue of 64 KB-128 KB of 16-B copies per SM becomes the limit, TMA would be the next step.

Descriptor k-advance inside a 128B-swizzle atom (+32 B start, base offset 0) follows CUTLASS / DeepGEMM and the audit; a wrong hardware model would fail the one-hot validation (path INVALID, r6 / pw23 kept), not the run.
16-B alignment: out is allocated by kernel_fn; a misaligned x is cloned in _rscall (rwrun would return -11).
